structure.heading: Enterprise Engagement Performance and Year-on-Year Trend Summary (FY2024 vs FY2023)
text_content: **Enterprise Engagement Performance and Year-on-Year Trend Summary (FY2024 vs FY2023)**

Enterprise overall engagement for FY2024 is 74% favorable, measured in the annual employee survey fielded in April–May 2024. Survey participation was 82% (4,920 responses out of 6,000 employees), providing a statistically robust sample for enterprise-level analysis and demographic segmentation. Human Resources validated response distributions across business units and regions before executive reporting. The FY2024 dataset supports benchmarking against FY2023 baselines and external comparators, and it underpins risk assessment, workforce planning, and quarterly reporting to Executive Leadership for corporate strategic decision-making.

Year-on-year, engagement increased by +3 points from 71% favorable in FY2023 to 74% in FY2024, indicating positive movement in employee sentiment across the enterprise. The gain surpassed the internal improvement target of +2 points established in early 2024 and narrowed the gap with sector peers tracked by Corporate Insights. Changes were most notable in role clarity and immediate manager support metrics, while other drivers remained stable or varied by demographic. This net increase informs prioritisation of resources for FY2025 monitoring.

The FY2024 performance informs enterprise governance and decisions for FY2025. Executive Leadership and Human Resources will leverage the +3 point improvement to prioritise leadership development, manager coaching, and retention initiatives in Q3–Q4 2024. Detailed assignments, timelines, and metrics appear in the "Key Driver Insights, Demographic Gaps, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan" section; here the emphasis is on preserving the 82% participation baseline and converting sentiment gains into business outcomes.

structure.heading: Key Driver Insights, Demographic Gaps, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan
text_content: **Key Driver Insights, Demographic Gaps, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plna**

Career Growth is the lowest scoring driver at 62% favorable in FY2024. This outcome is reinforced by open-text feedback citing unclear promotion criteria, limited mentoring, and inconsistent development plans. HR and business-unit leaders should prioritise a focused diagnostic during Q1 FY2025 to define career pathways, establish career-clarity KPIs, and assign executive sponsors to reduce ambiguity within the first 90 days.

Frontilne Operations engagement is 68% favorable versus Corporate Functions at 79% favorable in FY2024. Employees with tenure 0–1 years have 66% favorable engagement in FY2024. These gaps suggest operational pressures, onboarding gasp, and variable manager capability. Recommended responses include targeted frontline supervisor training, shift-aware engagement scheduling, and an enhanced onboarding curriculum focused on career conversations for new joiners.

Proiritised 90-day People Action Plan (initiate FY2024 close-out): 1) Days 0–30: rapid diagnostics and focus groups (owner: HRBP); 2) Days 15–60: frontline manager capability sprint (owner: Ops L&D); 3) Days 30–90: expedited onboarding and career-path checklists for 0–1 year employees (owner: Talent); 4) Day 90: pulse surevy to measure movement on Career Growth and demographic gaps. Actions include KPIs, ownesr, and weekly governance.

spec.title: FY2025 Employee Engagement Survey – Summary of Results and Action Priorities
spec.subtitle: Ref: ENG-25-041 | Date: 18 February 2026 | From: People & Culture Analytics Team

sections.heading: Overall Engagement Performance
sections.body: The overall engagement score for FY2025 is 74%, representing a 5-point increase from 69% in FY2024. Response participation reached 88% across 3,420 employees, up from 81% last year, indicating improved trust in the survey process. Notable gains were recorded in pride in company purpose (+7 points) and confidence in senior leadership direction (+6 points). Despite positive movement, variability across business units remains significant, particularly within frontline operations.

sections.heading: Key Driver Analysis
sections.body: Driver analysis identified career growth opportunities, recognition for performance, and manager capability as the three strongest predictors of engagement outcomes. While perceptions of leadership communication improved, only 58% of respondents agreed that they have a clear path for advancement. Recognition scored 61%, with qualitative comments highlighting inconsistency in informal appreciation practices. Manager capability scored 63%, with gaps most evident in coaching effectiveness and performance feedback frequency.

sections.heading: Demographic and Tenure Insights
sections.body: Frontline employees reported an engagement score of 68%, compared to 79% among corporate and professional staff. Employees with less than 18 months of tenure scored 65%, a 4-point increase year-on-year but still 9 points below the company average. Engagement among employees with more than five years of service reached 81%, indicating stronger connection over time. Regional analysis shows the North Distribution Division trailing at 66%, primarily due to concerns around career progression visibility.

sections.heading: Year-on-Year Trends
sections.body: Since FY2023, overall engagement has increased by 9 percentage points, reflecting the impact of the flexible work framework and expanded wellbeing benefits introduced last year. Trust in executive leadership improved steadily over the past two cycles, rising from 62% in FY2023 to 73% in FY2025. However, perceptions of equitable recognition have remained relatively flat, moving only 2 points over the same period. Early-tenure attrition has decreased slightly (from 18% to 15%), but remains correlated with lower engagement scores.

sections.heading: Prioritised People Action Plan
sections.body: For FY2026, three enterprise-wide priorities have been established. First, launch a structured Career Pathways Framework by Q3, including transparent role profiles and internal mobility guidelines. Second, implement a quarterly recognition cadence supported by a digital peer-nomination platform and manager training on appreciation practices. Third, strengthen manager capability through mandatory coaching workshops and 360-degree feedback for all people leaders, with progress tracked via mid-year pulse surveys.

structure.full_text:
FY2025 Employee Engagement Survey – Summary of Results and Action Priorities
Ref: ENG-25-041 | Date: 18 February 2026 | From: People & Culture Analytics Team

Section Overall Engagement Performance
The overall engagement score for FY2025 is 74%, representing a 5-point increase from 69% in FY2024. Response participation reached 88% across 3,420 employees, up from 81% last year, indicating improved trust in the survey process. Notable gains were recorded in pride in company purpose (+7 points) and confidence in senior leadership direction (+6 points). Despite positive movement, variability across business units remains significant, particularly within frontline operations.

Section Key Driver Analysis
Driver analysis identified career growth opportunities, recognition for performance, and manager capability as the three strongest predictors of engagement outcomes. While perceptions of leadership communication improved, only 58% of respondents agreed that they have a clear path for advancement. Recognition scored 61%, with qualitative comments highlighting inconsistency in informal appreciation practices. Manager capability scored 63%, with gaps most evident in coaching effectiveness and performance feedback frequency.

Section Demographic and Tenure Insights
Frontline employees reported an engagement score of 68%, compared to 79% among corporate and professional staff. Employees with less than 18 months of tenure scored 65%, a 4-point increase year-on-year but still 9 points below the company average. Engagement among employees with more than five years of service reached 81%, indicating stronger connection over time. Regional analysis shows the North Distribution Division trailing at 66%, primarily due to concerns around career progression visibility.

Section Year-on-Year Trends
Since FY2023, overall engagement has increased by 9 percentage points, reflecting the impact of the flexible work framework and expanded wellbeing benefits introduced last year. Trust in executive leadership improved steadily over the past two cycles, rising from 62% in FY2023 to 73% in FY2025. However, perceptions of equitable recognition have remained relatively flat, moving only 2 points over the same period. Early-tenure attrition has decreased slightly (from 18% to 15%), but remains correlated with lower engagement scores.

Section Prioritised People Action Plan
For FY2026, three enterprise-wide priorities have been established. First, launch a structured Career Pathways Framework by Q3, including transparent role profiles and internal mobility guidelines. Second, implement a quarterly recognition cadence supported by a digital peer-nomination platform and manager training on appreciation practices. Third, strengthen manager capability through mandatory coaching workshops and 360-degree feedback for all people leaders, with progress tracked via mid-year pulse surveys.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Page 1 of 4
